md_neptune_buttress.blurb: Neptune Buttress is one of the numbered buttresses strung along the clifftop above Cumberland, in the Cumberland Narrows (Lover's Leap) cliff band. Ten routes here, seven of them top-rope and three trad, run from an easy 5.2 scramble through the middle 5th-class grades up to a single 5.10, with most of the lines in the 5.6 to 5.9 range. That makes it a reasonable stop for newer leaders and top-rope parties alike. Most climbs have a couple of stars, and the slabby character suggests footwork over power. Reach the base by walking the clifftop trail and downclimbing at the north end of the buttress.

md_pillar_the.blurb: The Pillar is a compact block of white quartzite on Sugarloaf Mountain in Frederick County, sitting just beyond Middle Earth on the same woods path from the West View lot. Ten routes, six top-rope and four trad, cover a wide spread: one very easy line, a cluster of mid 5th-class climbs, and a few harder ones that reach into the low 5.12 range. The lines are short, and the rock is sharp, so protect your rope at the edges. Tree cover keeps it shaded in summer, though it stays damp for a day or two after rain. It is popular in season, so expect to share it.

md_downstream_slab_aka_snowflake_face.blurb: Downstream Slab, also called Snowflake Face, is a boulder face on the downstream side of the Chaos Roof boulder, in the Northwest Branch bouldering area just north of Washington, DC. It holds ten problems, mostly V2 to V6, with the bulk around V4, and a mix of crimpy face climbing, traverses and a dyno. Landings are fairly flat, which makes it a comfortable place to boulder alone, but the small crimps can feel sharp on tender skin. Chaos Roof sits a short walk past a few other boulders from the parking lot, and the area is busy with hikers on weekends.
